title: Governed publication across clients: the JS SDK proposes, the honua admin CLI's API-key approval is refused, a person approves in a Console session, the .NET SDK verifies
promise: A publication the JS SDK proposes is only published after a person approves it in a Console password session with the proposal's review capability. The typed admin CLI cannot approve with an API key: the proposer's own approval and the approver key's approval are both refused with 403, the latter with the server's human-approval refusal. The CLI then reads the proposal resolved by that person's session, and the .NET SDK sees exactly the approved version and content at the final publication.

steps.description: As the proposer, create a map package draft bound to the fixture's sites layer; the server validates it.
Save the draft as an immutable content version.
Request publication of the saved version at the fixture route; the server records a proposal awaiting approval.
The proposer tries to approve its own proposal with the typed admin CLI; the command fails with 403 and the proposal is still awaiting approval.

The approver tries to approve with its admin:approve API key through the typed admin CLI; the command fails with the server's 403 that requires a live interactive browser session, and the proposal is still awaiting approval.

steps.api: Console password session: open approval-review, approve with the review capability (e2e/harness/lib/human_approval.py)
steps.description: A person signs in to a Console password session over HTTPS, opens the proposal's approval review and approves with its review capability; the server records the console-interactive-password channel.

steps.api: honua admin operate getOperationProposal --profile approver (until terminal)
steps.description: Read the proposal with the typed admin CLI until it is terminal (bounded): it succeeded, was requested by the proposer and resolved by the person's Console session.
Poll the publication request the JS SDK created to Active; it carries the final publication URL at the fixture route.
Read the content item's pointers through the .NET SDK; the published pointer is the version the JS SDK saved.
Read the published version through the .NET SDK; its map body and content hash equal what the JS SDK saved.
Read the final publication URL through the .NET SDK; it serves the approved version's content.
